messages:
marta: Quick report — found a puzzling typing regression when our TS SDK is bundled for Edge runtimes. Generic overloads stop inferring and callers see `any`. Minimal repro attached in a tiny sample app.

devon: oh no. can you paste the minimal example here?

marta: sure. gist of it: 
```ts
// api.ts (library)
export function call<T>(path: string, opts?: { payload?: T }): Promise<{ data: T }>;
export function call(path: string, opts?: any) { /* impl */ }
```
When bundling an ESM build for a worker (Vite -> esbuild targeting 'edge') `call<User>` becomes `any` at the callsite. In our Node/CJS tests it types correctly.

sandeep: interesting. sounds like either the bundler's type path resolution or the emitted declaration shapes are different. Which tsconfig + build pipeline are you using?

marta: tsconfig: module=esnext, moduleResolution=bundler, declaration=true, emitDeclarationOnly during build. bundling with Vite 5 + esbuild target webworker. I can reproduce both when importing from dist (compiled d.ts) and when path-importing the src files through tsconfig paths.

elena: i've seen inference break when overloads are flattened during .d.ts generation or when the consuming project uses a different resolution strategy (node16 vs bundler). Does switching moduleResolution to node16 help locally?

marta: tried node16 and classic, no luck. Weirdly, if I change the exported API to a single generic implementation (no overload signatures) inference is preserved in the edge bundle. So the shape of the declaration seems to matter.

devon: does the implementation signature use `any` while the declaration uses `unknown` anywhere? `unknown` can sometimes block inference through overloads.

marta: we do prefer `unknown` in a few helpers. swapping to `any` in the tiny repro made inference appear correct, but we don't want to globally relax types.

sandeep: another angle: check package.json exports/types fields. Some bundlers will pick up an alternate entry that points to a converted file. If dist/ d.ts were post-processed (rollup plugin, dts bundler) overload shapes can collapse.

marta: good call. locally importing from `dist` vs `src` differs. importing from `src` keeps inference; `dist` breaks. So publishing pipeline likely reshapes the declarations.

elena: tactic: keep `declaration: true` but ensure the generated .d.ts mirrors the source overloads exactly. Try `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` from source tree and avoid bundling d.ts with third-party tools. Also set `declarationMap: true` to aid debugging.

devon: parallel runtime issue I noticed: our retry wrapper behaves slightly differently on Edge fetch vs Node fetch polyfill, sometimes returning undefined on exhausted retries. That union (`Response | undefined`) can cause generic return types to widen and confuse inference in overload contexts.

marta: yes — saw that too. On Edge the adapter wraps fetch errors differently so the wrapped API type is not identical between environments. Combined with overload flattening it's a mess.

sandeep: recommended fix: introduce a tiny platform-agnostic adapter at the SDK boundary with a consistent typed signature (e.g., PlatformFetch -> Promise<ResponseLike> always). Keep that type stable and exported in types so consumer d.ts don't see env-specific unions.

elena: plus CI: add an integration job that installs the built package into a fresh small-app template, runs Vite + typecheck in an edge-emulation mode. That will catch regressions early.

marta: plan I'm proposing: 1) add typed fetch adapter with stable ResponseLike; 2) change packaging so we ship tsc-emitted .d.ts without bundling-transform; 3) add docs in the onboarding template about moduleResolution/bundler caveats; 4) CI job to build + install + typecheck small-app (Vite/EsmEdge).

devon: sounds good. can you open an issue and drop the repro?

build-bot: @marta opened GH issue #1251: "Edge ESM bundle + overload inference lost — probable d.ts packaging mismatch" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1251 :gear:

marta: done. i'll push a minimal repo and a short writeup. Also adding the workaround note in the SDK migration guide: prefer single generic exports if you expect some consumers to run edge-bundled code until we fix the packaging.

sandeep: one more debugging tip: in the consumer project run `tsc --traceResolution` to see which .d.ts is actually being consumed. Helps pinpoint if it's the compiled file or a path-mapped source file.

elena: tiny nit: avoid `moduleResolution: bundler` in our example templates for now; it's still evolving and can produce surprising results with complex types.

marta: thanks all — i'll iterate on the PR for packaging + adapter and link to the issue and the onboarding note. :thumbsup:
